chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Ahmad, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Saffar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from his father, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Mihan ibn Muhammad, from Sa'd al-Iskafi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said:

The one who drinks wine or an intoxicant, his prayer will not be accepted for forty mornings, and if he returns, Allah will make him drink from the clay of lunacy. I said: And what is the clay of lunacy? He said: A pus that comes out from the genitals of adulteresses.
ai.seo_question: What is the consequence of drinking wine on one's prayer according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Ma'ani al-Akhbar* establishes the legal consequence of consuming intoxicants, linking spiritual rejection of prayer to physical punishment. The term 'taynat khabal' (clay of lunacy) is interpreted here as the pus of adulteresses, a specific exegetical view that connects the internal corruption of the drinker to the external impurity of the adulteress, reflecting the Shia tradition of detailed bodily and spiritual purification. This ruling underscores the severity of *khamr* not just as a legal violation but as a source of spiritual and physical defilement.
